questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heterophyllous development in response to environment is an example of which of the following phenomena ?
questions.solution:
Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity.

Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur is an example of plasticity in response to phases of life, whereas heterophylly in buttercup is an example of plasticity in response to the environment. In buttercup, the leaves of juvenile plants and mature plants are different in shape, and similarly, the leaves of submerged plants are highly dissected compared to the broad leaves of aerial plants.

Answer: Plasticity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Length of the stem at time 0 is $20$ cm. The arithmetic growth rate is $30$ cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the $7^{th}$ day ?
questions.solution:
The equation for arithmetic growth is given by:

$L_t = L_0 + rt$

Where:
$L_t$ is the length at time $t$
$L_0$ is the initial length at time $t = 0$
$r$ is the arithmetic growth rate
$t$ is the time

Given:
$L_0 = 20$ cm
$r = 30$ cm/day
$t = 7$ days

Substituting the given values into the equation:

$L_7 = 20 + 30 \times 7$

$L_7 = 20 + 210$

$L_7 = 230$ cm

questions.q: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage ?
questions.solution:
Gibberellins promote internode elongation just prior to flowering in rosette plants like cabbage, beet, and many other plants with a rosette habit. This phenomenon is known as bolting.

Ethephon is a source of ethylene, which promotes fruit ripening and abscission.

Abscisic acid acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and stress hormone.

Indole butyric acid is a synthetic auxin widely used to induce rooting in stem cuttings.

Answer: Gibberellin

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation ?
questions.solution:
The period of growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation.

The cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei. Their cell walls are primary in nature, thin, and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

The cells in the phase of elongation are characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

Therefore, large conspicuous nuclei are a characteristic of meristematic cells, not cells in the phase of elongation.

Answer: Large conspicuous nuclei

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phenomenon which is influenced by auxin and also played a major role in its discovery :
questions.solution: Auxin influences phototropism, i.e., the growth of the plant in response to light stimulus and this phenomenon played a major role in its discovery. Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin observed that the coleoptile of canary grass responded to the unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism). They concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the source of auxin and was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which hormone promotes internode / petiole elongation in deep water rice?
questions.solution:
Ethylene (${C}_{2}{H}_{4}$) is a gaseous hormone which is mainly involved in the fruit ripening process. The major physiological effects of ethylene are:

  • Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants.
  • Ethylene also promotes root growth and root hair formation, thus helping the plants to increase their absorption surface.
  • Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, sprouting of potato tubers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
questions.solution: Some seeds fail to germinate even when external conditions are favorable. Such seeds are dormant and are controlled by endogenous conditions within the seed itself. Impermeable and hard seed coat; phenolic acids, para-ascorbic acid; immature embryos, and the presence of chemical inhibitors such as abscisic acids are some reasons which cause seed dormancy. The effect of such inhibitory substances can be removed by the application of certain chemicals like gibberellic acid and nitrates or by subjecting the seeds to chilling conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process of growth is maximum during
questions.solution:
SIGMOID CURVE/ GROWTH CURVE: A plant exhibit differential growth during its life cycle. In the case of herbaceous plants, the growth is exhibited in three steps, i.e. lag phase, log phase, and phase.

Lag phase: It refers to the first stage of the life cycle of a plant. In this stage, the growth is negligible.

Log phase: During the log phase, the plant exhibits logarithmic in the size. It is the phase, in which maximum growth is seen.

Steady phase: During the steady phase growth ceases, and it results in an S-shaped curve called sigmoid curve/growth curve.

questions.solution: The gibberellins, cytokinins and auxins are found to be growth stimulators, whereas ethylene and abscisic acid are determined as growth inhibitors. The function of cytokinin is the stimulation of cell division, growth of lateral buds and apical dominance. Functions of gibberellins are to stimulate stem elongation. Auxin and ethylene are responsible for the flowering and fruiting in pineapple.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: You are given tissue with its potential for differentiation in artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
questions.solution: Auxins and cytokinins are used in the development of root and shoot in a culture medium (respectively). In the root meristem, auxin induces the meristematic cell division, whereas cytokinin promotes the cell to switch from the meristematic to a differentiated state through inhibiting auxin signaling.

questions.q: What causes a green plant exposed to the light on only one side, to bend toward the source of light as it grows?
options: Green plants need light to perform photosynthesis.
Green plants seek light because they are phototropic.
Light stimulates plant cells on the lighted side to grow faster.
Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating greater cell elongation there.
questions.solution: Auxins accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating grater cell elongation there. Since auxins move from morphological apex to morphological base therefore gets accumulated on the shaded side. Thus plants exposed to the light on only one side bends towards the source of light. It is also due to the tropic movement of auxins which causes phototropism and geotropism in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Typical growth curve in plants is:
questions.solution:
The growth pattern of cells, organisms is uniform under favourable conditions & a typical growth curve in plants is sigmoidal. Thus following phases of growth are recognized.

(i) Lag phase: In the lag period the growth is slow. It represents the formative or cell division phase.

(ii) Log phase: Also called as exponential phase. During this phase, growth is maximum & most rapid. It represents the cell elongation phase.

(iii) Steady or stationary phase: It represents the cell maturation phase.

Time taken in growth phases (mainly log phase) is called a grand period of growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Dr F. Went noted that if coleoptile tips were removed and placed on agar for one hour, the agar would produce a bending when placed on one side of freshly- cut coleoptile stumps. Of what significance is this experiment?
options: It made possible the isolation and exact identification of auxin.
It is the basis for quantitative determination of small amounts of growth- promoting substances.
It supports the hypothesis that IAA is auxin.
It demonstrated polar movements of auxins
questions.solution:
Darwin and his son observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source. This is called phototropism. They performed series of experiments which concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile. F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings and concluded that phototropism of oat seedlings occur. They also concluded that phototropism in the tips of coleoptiles is due to the polar movement of auxin in the stem.
So, the correct answer is 'it demonstrated polar movements of auxins'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as:
questions.solution: After the divisions are over, differentiation of a cell leads to the attribution of a specialised function. For example the cell forms mesophyll cells. When mesophyll cells are cultured, they form callus, which is an undifferentiated mass of cells. Thus, this is a process of dedifferentiation. The cell of callus can re-differentiate to form organs, or any tissue.

questions.q: A few normal seedlings of tomato were kept in a dark room. After a few days, they were found to have become white-colored like albinos, Which of the following terms will you use to describe them?
questions.solution:
Etiolation is a phenomenon present in plants that are due to complete or partial absence of light. Skotomorphogenesis is the other name seed germination in absence of light, which leads to etiolation.
Etiolation causes some typical changes in the morphology of the plant (seedling). This happens primarily due to the likelihood of reaching the source of light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following growth regulators is known as stress hormone?
questions.solution:
Abscisic acid (ABA) is also known as the stress hormone, is produced during drought, water stress, and any other environmental stress conditions.
This hormone is a dextro-rotatory sesquiterpene-derivative and is synthesized from xanthophylls via the mevalonic acid pathway in the plants.
This hormone is a plant growth inhibitor. When the plant is in water stress, more amount of ABA is synthesized and secreted from the leaves. The transport of this hormone is via diffusion or even via conducting elements. It is an anti-transpirant as it closes the stomata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tissue culture technique can produce infinite number or new plants from a small parental tissue. The economic importance of the technique is in raising:
options: genetically uniform population identical to the original parent.
variants through picking up somaclonal variations
questions.solution:
The technique to generate whole plant from an explant with in vitro condition on a suitable synthetic medium is called tissue culture. We can produce several plants. Genetic constitution of all plants is same, leading to identical population to the original parent. Disease free plants can be produced in large number.
Related Theory
In Tissue culture, culture of an excised part in an aseptic culture medium to form a callus, in which differentiation of root and shoot buds is induced by providing suitable combination of auxins and cytokinin then the plantlets are transferred to the soil to develop into mature plants. The technique is based on the property of totipotency of plant cell which means that any cell from any part of the plant can be used to generate a whole new plant.

Photoperiodism is a phenomenon that describes the requirement of light to stimulate the flowering on a vegetative shoot.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Senescence as an active developmental cellular process in the growth and functioning of a flowering plant, is indicated in
questions.solution:
Senescence can be defined as "the sum of deteriorative processes, which naturally terminate the functional life of an organism". Senescence is not confined only to whole plant, it may be limited to a particular plant organ such as leaf and flower or cells such as phloem and xylem. Abscission is natural shedding of leaves, foliage branches, fruits, floral parts etc. According to Leopold (1967) abscission is a senescence phenomenon. Senescence as an active developmental cellular process in the growth and functioning of a flowering plant, is indicated in leaf abscission.
Whole plant senescence also known as overall senescence occurs in annuals (eg, rice, wheat, gram, mustard) biennials (eg, henbane) or perennials.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fruit and leaf drop at early stages can be prevented by the application of
questions.solution:
Among the various types of growth promoters in plants, Auxins, Gibberellins and Cytokinins are most common and well characterized. The Auxin delay abscission of leaves and fruits at early stages. Whenever leaf or fruit fall occurs, the organ concerned stops producing auxin. However, it promotes abscission of order, mature leaves, and fruit. Abscision is a natural phenomenon of old parts. Primarily this is accomplished by Abscisic acid hormone (ABA). NAA prevents fruit drop in tomato; 2,4-D prevents fruit drop in Citrus.

Cytokinins are mainly involved in cell division. Gibberellins are mainly involved in stem internode elongation.

The long chain fatty acids are then broken down by successive removal of two carbon fragments in the process of $\beta$-oxidation.
Peroxisomes are present in all photosynthetic cells of higher plants in etiolated leaf tissue. It is the site of hydrogen peroxide metabolism and glycolate cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One set of the plant was grown at 12 hours day and 12 hours night period cycles and it flowered while in the other set night phase was interrupted by flash of light and it did not produce flower. Under which one of the following categories will you place this plant?
questions.solution:
Short day plants (SDP) require a relatively short-day light period (usually $8-10$ hours) and a continuous dark period of about 14-16 hours for subsequent flowering. If these plants are exposed to day lengths in excess of this critical point, they continue growing vegetatively and do not show flowering. Most of the winter flowering plants belong to this category. For example, Rice, coffee, soybean, tobacco, sugarcane, strawberry and chrysanthemum.
Related Theory
In long that plants, it was found that they can flower even under short day conditions, if a flash of light is provided to the plant during the long dark period. Thus, periods of darkness have inhibitory effect on flowering in these plants.

In stationary phase, the growth curve begins to decline as the available nutrients become depleted and waste products start to accumulate. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the reason for the formation of embryoid from pollen grain in tissue culture-medium?
questions.solution:
Cellular totipotency is the ability of a single cell to differentiate into all cell types and to organize them to give rise to an entire organism in a suitable culture medium with appropriate temperature and aeration. Spores and zygotes are some of the examples of totipotent cells.
Related Theory
In 1902, Professor Gottlieb Haberlandt, proposed the idea of Totipotency. He said that every living cell of the plant body can regenerate the entire plant body because it is obtained from the fertilized egg and contains genetic data.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Importance of day length in flowering of plants was first shown in
questions.solution: The phenomenon of photoperiodism was first discovered by Garner and Allard (1920, 1922). They observed that maryland mammoth variety of tobacco could be made to flower only by reducing the light hours with artificial darkening. On the basis of photoperiodic response to flowering, plants have been divided into short day plants (tobacco), long day plant (eg, wheat, hanbane), short-long day plants (eg, Campanula), long-short day plants (eg, Bryophyllum), intermediate plants (eg, wild kidney bean) and day neutral plants (eg, cotton).

questions.q: Opening of floral buds into flowers, is a type of:
questions.solution:
The opening of floral buds and the change into a flower is a nastic movement. It is a type of autonomic movement of growth in which the direction of the movement isindependent of the direction of the stimulus. In fact, the response is determined by the structure of the responsive organ and not by the opposite side.

questions.q: Differentiation of shoot is controlled by:
questions.solution:
A high cytokinin to auxin ratio triggers shoot formation but inhibits root induction, whereas, a low ratio produces the opposite effect. Plant growth regulators (cytokinin, auxin) are widely used to control differentiation in cultured plant cells and tissues.
Related Theory
In the root meristem, auxin induces the meristematic cell division, whereas cytokinin promotes the cell to swith from the meristematic to differentiated state through inhibiting auxin signalling. Auxin at low concentrations limits the action of cytokinin. An increase in cytokinin level counteracts this inhibitory effect and leads to an inhibition of auxin stgnalling. At higher concentrations of both hormones, these antagonistic interactions between cytokinin and auxin are absent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the formula for arithmetic growth given in the text?
questions.solution: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. Mathematically, it is expressed asLt = L0 + rt

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What role does oxygen play in plant growth?
options: It releases metabolic energy essential for growth activities
questions.solution: The plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement which in turn requires water. Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth. Thus, plant growth and further development is intimately linked to the water status of the plant. Water also provides the medium for enzymatic activities needed for growth. Oxygen helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities.

questions.q: Length of a plant root at time 0 is 25 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 15 cm per day. What will be the length of the root at the end of the 10th day?
questions.solution: In arithmetic growth, length increases at a constant rate. Final length = initial length + (growth rate × number of days) = 25 + (15 × 10) = 25 + 150 = 175 cm. Hence the length of the root at the end of the 10th day is 175 cm.

This form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the open form of growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Period of growth is generally divided into two phases
2. Root apex represents maturation phase of growth
3. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei.
4. The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation.
5. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.
questions.solution: The period of growth is generally divided into three phases, namely, meristematic, elongation and maturation. The constantly dividing cells, both at the root apex and the shoot apex, represent the meristematic phase of growth. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei. The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.

The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.

Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Stationary phase is a phase marked by increased division of cells
2. Root elongation at constant rate is an example of arithmetic growth
3. In geometric growth the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and it increases rapidly thereafter – at a logarithmic rate (log or exponential phase).
4. Both the progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide and continue to do so.
5. With limited nutrient supply, the growth slows down leading to a stationary phase.
questions.solution: The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate. Let us now see what happens in geometrical growth. In most systems, the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and it increases rapidly thereafter – at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase). Here, both the progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide and continue to do so. However, with limited nutrient supply, the growth slows down leading to a stationary phase

4. The phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment (Figure 13.9). This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A specific plant growth regulator is known to promote nutrient mobilisation and delay leaf senescence. Consider the following statements regarding this regulator:
(A) It helps to overcome apical dominance.
(B) It is synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs.
(C) It promotes bolting in rosette plants.
(D) It induces parthenocarpy in tomatoes.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The plant growth regulator that promotes nutrient mobilisation and delays leaf senescence is Cytokinin.

Statement (A) is correct: Cytokinins help to overcome apical dominance.

Statement (B) is correct: Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, such as root apices, developing shoot buds, and young fruits.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Gibberellins, not cytokinins, promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in rosette plants like beet and cabbages.

Statement (D) is incorrect: Auxins are widely applied to induce parthenocarpy in tomatoes.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (A) and (B), are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.q: A farmer wishes to increase the yield of his sugarcane crop. He is advised to spray a specific plant growth regulator that increases the length of the stem, thereby increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Which of the following phytohormones should be sprayed?

Answer: Gibberellic acid

Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true.

Match List-I with List-II regarding seed dormancy and its removal.

(B) Gibberellic acid(II) Endogenous chemical inhibitor
(C) Impermeable seed coat(III) Temperature treatment to break dormancy
(D) Chilling conditions(IV) Physical cause of dormancy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Seed dormancy can be caused by physical barriers such as an impermeable and hard seed coat (C matches IV) or by endogenous chemical inhibitors such as para-ascorbic acid, abscisic acid, and phenolic acids (A matches II).

This dormancy can be overcome by applying specific chemicals like gibberellic acid and nitrates (B matches I) or by subjecting the seeds to chilling conditions, which serves as a temperature treatment to break dormancy (D matches III).

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A gardener sprays the plant growth regulator $2,4$-D on a lawn that contains a mixture of mature grasses and broad-leaved weeds. What will be the specific outcome of this application?
options: It will kill the mature grasses and leave the broad-leaved weeds unaffected.
It will kill the broad-leaved weeds while leaving the mature grasses unaffected.
It will act as a non-selective herbicide and kill both the grasses and the broad-leaved weeds.
It will promote the rapid vegetative growth of both the grasses and the broad-leaved weeds.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, $2,4$-D ($2,4$-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a weedicide.

It selectively kills dicotyledonous (broad-leaved) weeds but does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants (such as grasses).

Therefore, the broad-leaved weeds will be destroyed, allowing the gardener to maintain a weed-free lawn, while the mature grasses will remain unaffected.

Answer: It will kill the broad-leaved weeds while leaving the mature grasses unaffected.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cells of the secondary cortex (phelloderm) and cork (phellem) are considered as redifferentiated tissues.

Reason (R): They are formed by the division of cork cambium, a dedifferentiated tissue, and these new cells subsequently lose the capacity to divide to perform specific functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because phelloderm (secondary cortex) and phellem (cork) are secondary tissues that have matured and lost their capacity to divide.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact explanation for (A). Cork cambium (phellogen) is a secondary meristem formed by the dedifferentiation of mature parenchyma cells. When the cells produced by the division of this dedifferentiated cork cambium mature and lose their capacity to divide to perform specific functions (like protection), the process is called redifferentiation. Therefore, the resulting tissues (cork and secondary cortex) are called redifferentiated tissues.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A student observes a longitudinal section of a growing root tip under a microscope. If the observation moves strictly proximally from the region of meristematic activity towards the mature base, which of the following sequences correctly represents the predominant cellular features encountered?
options: Maximal wall thickening $\rightarrow$ Increased vacuolation $\rightarrow$ Large conspicuous nuclei
Large conspicuous nuclei $\rightarrow$ Increased vacuolation $\rightarrow$ Maximal wall thickening
Large conspicuous nuclei $\rightarrow$ Maximal wall thickening $\rightarrow$ Increased vacuolation
Increased vacuolation $\rightarrow$ Large conspicuous nuclei $\rightarrow$ Maximal wall thickening
questions.solution:
The period of growth is divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation. In a root tip, moving proximally (away from the tip) from the region of meristematic activity, one encounters the phase of elongation followed by the phase of maturation.

The cells in the meristematic region are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei.

The cells in the elongation zone (proximal to the meristem) are characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

The cells in the maturation zone (further proximal to the elongation zone) attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

Therefore, the correct spatial sequence of cellular features moving proximally is: Large conspicuous nuclei $\rightarrow$ Increased vacuolation $\rightarrow$ Maximal wall thickening.

Answer: Large conspicuous nuclei $\rightarrow$ Increased vacuolation $\rightarrow$ Maximal wall thickening

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A vegetable vendor wants to keep harvested leafy vegetables fresh and green for a longer duration before selling them in the market. Which of the following plant growth regulators should be applied to achieve this by delaying leaf senescence?
questions.solution:
Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. Therefore, applying cytokinins helps in keeping leafy vegetables fresh and green for a longer duration.

Ethylene and abscisic acid are senescence-promoting hormones, which would cause the leaves to yellow and degrade faster. Gibberellic acid is used to delay senescence in fruits on trees, but cytokinin is specifically associated with delaying leaf senescence via nutrient mobilisation.

Answer: Cytokinin

Assertion: The decapitated (tip-removed) coleoptile of canary grass continues to bend towards a unilateral light source.
Reason: The tip of the coleoptile is the site of production of a transmittable influence that causes the bending of the entire coleoptile.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The Assertion is false because the decapitated coleoptile of canary grass fails to bend towards a unilateral light source. Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed that the tip of the coleoptile perceives the light stimulus.

The Reason is true because they concluded that the tip of the coleoptile is the site of a transmittable influence (later identified as auxin) that causes the bending of the entire coleoptile. When the tip is removed, this influence is absent, and phototropism does not occur.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Under certain conditions, living differentiated cells in plants regain the capacity of division. The formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of which of the following processes?
questions.solution:
In plants, living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed dedifferentiation.

The formation of secondary meristems like interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells are classic examples of dedifferentiation in natural plant growth.

Differentiation (or maturation) is the process where meristematic cells mature to perform specific functions. Redifferentiation occurs when dedifferentiated cells again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions.

Answer: Dedifferentiation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the plant growth regulator first isolated by F.W. Went from the tips of oat coleoptiles:

I. It was first isolated from human urine.
II. It promotes apical dominance in higher plants.
III. NAA and 2,4-D are its natural derivatives isolated from plants.
IV. It is widely used to kill monocotyledonous weeds.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The plant growth regulator first isolated by F.W. Went from the tips of oat (Avena) coleoptiles is auxin.

Statement I is correct: Auxin was first isolated from human urine.

Statement II is correct: In higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance, which is mediated by auxins.

Statement III is incorrect: IAA and IBA are natural auxins isolated from plants, whereas NAA and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins.

Statement IV is incorrect: 2,4-D is widely used as a herbicide to kill dicotyledonous weeds, but it does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the developmental status of plant tissues.

List IList II
A. Apical meristem1. Product of dedifferentiation
B. Tracheary element2. Product of redifferentiation
C. Cork cambium3. Undifferentiated tissue
D. Secondary xylem4. Product of differentiation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Apical meristem is a primary meristem and consists of actively dividing, undifferentiated cells (A-3).

Tracheary elements (like tracheids and vessels) are formed when cells derived from root and shoot apical meristems mature and lose their protoplasm to perform specific functions. This process is differentiation (B-4).

Cork cambium is a secondary meristem formed when living differentiated cells (like cortical parenchyma) regain the capacity to divide. This is dedifferentiation (C-1).

Secondary xylem is formed when cells derived from the vascular cambium (a dedifferentiated tissue) lose their capacity to divide and mature. This is redifferentiation (D-2).

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the phases of plant growth in List-I with their corresponding cellular characteristics in List-II.

List-IList-II
A. Meristematic phase1. Maximal wall thickening
B. Elongation phase2. Abundant plasmodesmatal connections
C. Maturation phase3. Increased vacuolation
4. Dedifferentiation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The period of growth is divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation.

Meristematic phase (A) cells are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei, and have thin primary cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections (2).

Elongation phase (B) cells are characterised by increased vacuolation (3), cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

Maturation phase (C) cells attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening (1) and protoplasmic modifications.

Dedifferentiation (4) is a separate phenomenon where differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide, not a characteristic of the primary growth phases.

Therefore, the correct match is A-2, B-3, C-1.

Answer: A-2, B-3, C-1

questions.q:
A synthetic plant growth regulator 'X' is widely used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. It achieves this by selectively killing 'Y' weeds.

Identify 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.solution:
Auxins are classified into natural and synthetic types. IAA (Indole-3-acetic acid) and IBA are natural auxins, whereas NAA and $2,4$-D are synthetic auxins.

The synthetic auxin $2,4$-D is extensively used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns.

It acts as a selective weedicide that kills dicotyledonous weeds but does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. Thus, X is $2,4$-D and Y is Dicotyledonous.

Answer: X = $2,4$-D, Y = Dicotyledonous

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Some seeds fail to germinate even when external conditions like moisture, oxygen, and temperature are highly favourable.

Reason (R): Such seeds are under endogenous control due to factors like immature embryos or the presence of chemical inhibitors such as phenolic acids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because some seeds do not germinate even under favourable external conditions of moisture, oxygen, and temperature. This phenomenon is known as seed dormancy.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the Assertion. The failure to germinate under favourable external conditions is because the seeds are under endogenous control (conditions within the seed itself). These endogenous factors include impermeable and hard seed coats, immature embryos, and the presence of chemical inhibitors such as abscisic acid, phenolic acids, and para-ascorbic acid.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins can increase the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.
Reason (R): Gibberellins induce early flowering and seed formation in sugarcane, which leads to massive carbohydrate accumulation in the stems.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Sugarcanes store carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct.

Gibberellins increase the yield by promoting internode elongation, not by inducing flowering. In fact, inducing flowering in sugarcane would consume the stored sugars and reduce the yield. Therefore, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the investigation of callus proliferation in tobacco stems, Miller et al. identified and crystallised a cytokinesis-promoting active substance termed kinetin. Based on its chemical composition, this plant growth regulator is classified as:
questions.solution:
Miller et al. identified and crystallised kinetin, which is a cytokinesis-promoting active substance (a cytokinin).

According to the chemical composition of plant growth regulators, cytokinins like kinetin ($N^{6}$-furfurylamino purine) are modified purines, specifically adenine derivatives.

Indole compounds refer to auxins (e.g., IAA), terpenes refer to gibberellins (e.g., $GA_{3}$), and derivatives of carotenoids refer to abscisic acid (ABA).

Answer: An adenine derivative

Read the following statements regarding the physiological effects of plant growth regulators:
(A) Gibberellins speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.
(B) Spraying juvenile conifers with gibberellic acids hastens the maturity period.
(C) Gibberellins promote bolting in beet, cabbages and many plants with a rosette habit.
(D) In most situations, abscisic acid acts as an antagonist to gibberellins.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as GA3 is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.

Statement (B) is correct because spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, which leads to early seed production.

Statement (C) is correct as gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with a rosette habit.

Statement (D) is correct because in most situations, ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs (for example, in seed dormancy where ABA induces dormancy and GA breaks it).

Since all four statements are correct, the correct option is Four.

Answer: Four

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Decapitation (removal of shoot tips) is a widely applied technique in tea plantations and hedge-making.
Reason (R): Removal of the apical bud relieves lateral buds from apical dominance, which is otherwise maintained by auxins synthesized in the shoot apex.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In most higher plants, the growing apical bud produces auxins which inhibit the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds. This phenomenon is called apical dominance.

Decapitation, which is the removal of shoot tips, eliminates the main source of auxin. This relieves the lateral buds from apical dominance, allowing them to grow and form branches.

Because this promotes branching, decapitation is widely applied in tea plantations and hedge-making. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following combinations of cellular characteristics correctly describes the cells in the meristematic phase of plant growth?
options: Thick secondary cell walls, rich protoplasm, and increased vacuolation
Thin primary cellulosic cell walls, large conspicuous nuclei, and maximal wall thickening
Rich protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary cellulosic cell walls, and abundant plasmodesmata
Abundant plasmodesmatal connections, increased vacuolation, and new cell wall deposition
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the cells in the meristematic phase of growth are constantly dividing. They are characterised by being rich in protoplasm and possessing large conspicuous nuclei. Their cell walls are primary in nature, thin, and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

Increased vacuolation and new cell wall deposition are features of the elongation phase.

Maximal wall thickening is a characteristic feature of the maturation phase.

Therefore, only the combination of rich protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary cell walls, and abundant plasmodesmata correctly describes meristematic cells.

Answer: Rich protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary cellulosic cell walls, and abundant plasmodesmata

questions.q: In a foundational experiment on plant growth regulators, F. Skoog observed that a mass of undifferentiated cells (callus) proliferated when the nutrient medium was supplemented with auxin along with extracts of vascular tissues, yeast extract, or coconut milk. Which specific plant tissue was used in this observation?
questions.solution:
F. Skoog and his co-workers observed that from the internodal segments of tobacco stems, the callus proliferated only if, in addition to auxins, the nutrient medium was supplemented with extracts of vascular tissues, yeast extract, coconut milk or DNA.

Coleoptile tips of oat seedlings were used by F.W. Went for the discovery of auxin. Uninfected rice seedlings were used by E. Kurosawa in the discovery of gibberellic acid. Coleoptiles of canary grass were used by Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin for observing phototropism.

Answer: Internodal segments of tobacco stem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
During a specific phase of growth, certain plant cells lose their protoplasm and develop very strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to carry water under extreme tension.

Identify the developmental process involved and the specific cell type formed.
questions.solution:
The cells that lose their protoplasm and develop strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to carry water under extreme tension are the tracheary elements (tracheids and vessels) of the xylem.

The process by which cells derived from root apical and shoot apical meristems and cambium mature to perform specific functions is called differentiation. During this process, they undergo major structural changes, such as the loss of protoplasm to form dead, hollow tracheary elements.

Dedifferentiation is the regaining of division capacity by mature cells, while redifferentiation is the loss of division capacity by dedifferentiated cells. Sieve tube elements are phloem components that lack lignocellulosic walls and transport food, not water.

Answer: Differentiation ; Tracheary elements

questions.q: A certain plant growth regulator 'X' is known to promote internode elongation just prior to flowering in rosette plants like cabbage. Which of the following is another physiological effect or commercial application of the same plant growth regulator 'X'?

Promotes root growth and root hair formation
Speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry
questions.solution:
The plant growth regulator 'X' that promotes internode elongation just prior to flowering (a phenomenon known as bolting) in rosette plants like cabbage is Gibberellin.

Gibberellins have several other commercial applications, one of which is speeding up the malting process in the brewing industry (specifically $\text{GA}_{3}$).

Ethylene promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants and also promotes root growth and root hair formation. Auxins are widely used to induce parthenocarpy in tomatoes.

Answer: Speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry

questions.q: Which of the following plant growth regulators is responsible for breaking seed and bud dormancy, initiating germination in peanut seeds, and sprouting of potato tubers?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, and promotes the sprouting of potato tubers.

Abscisic acid (ABA) generally acts as a growth inhibitor and induces dormancy rather than breaking it. While Gibberellic acid is involved in breaking seed dormancy in certain cases, the specific examples of peanut seeds and potato tubers are directly attributed to ethylene. Cytokinins are primarily involved in cell division, overcoming apical dominance, and delaying senescence.

Answer: Ethylene

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Abscisic acid (ABA) is broadly considered to act as an antagonist to Gibberellic acids (GAs).
Reason (R): ABA stimulates the closure of stomata in the epidermis and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because Abscisic acid (ABA) acts as an antagonist to GAs. For example, ABA induces seed dormancy and inhibits germination, whereas GAs break seed dormancy and promote germination.

Reason (R) is also correct because ABA is known as the stress hormone; it stimulates the closure of stomata and increases plant tolerance to various stresses.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The antagonistic relationship between ABA and GAs is primarily based on their opposing roles in seed dormancy and germination, not on ABA's role in stomatal closure during stress.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.q: A farmer observes that his wheat crop is heavily infested with broad-leaved weeds. Which of the following plant growth regulators should he spray to eliminate the weeds without damaging the wheat crop?
questions.solution:
Wheat is a monocotyledonous crop, while the broad-leaved weeds are dicotyledonous.

According to NCERT, 2,4-D (a synthetic auxin) is widely used as a herbicide to kill dicotyledonous weeds and it does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.

Therefore, spraying 2,4-D will selectively eliminate the broad-leaved weeds without harming the wheat crop. Cytokinin, abscisic acid, and gibberellic acid do not possess this selective herbicidal property.

Answer: 2,4-D

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following anatomical events in plant development:

Event X: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully differentiated medullary ray cells.
Event Y: Formation of secondary xylem elements from the vascular cambium.
Event Z: Maturation of root apical meristem cells into root hair cells.

Identify the developmental processes that correspond to Events X, Y, and Z respectively.
options: X - Differentiation, Y - Dedifferentiation, Z - Redifferentiation
X - Dedifferentiation, Y - Redifferentiation, Z - Differentiation
X - Redifferentiation, Y - Dedifferentiation, Z - Differentiation
X - Dedifferentiation, Y - Differentiation, Z - Dedifferentiation
questions.solution:
Event X represents dedifferentiation. Living differentiated cells (medullary ray cells) regain the capacity to divide to form a meristem (interfascicular cambium).

Event Y represents redifferentiation. The cells produced by the dedifferentiated meristem (vascular cambium) lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions (secondary xylem).

Event Z represents differentiation. Cells derived from primary meristems (root apical meristem) undergo structural changes to mature into specific cells like root hair cells.

Thus, the correct sequence is X - Dedifferentiation, Y - Redifferentiation, Z - Differentiation.

Answer: X - Dedifferentiation, Y - Redifferentiation, Z - Differentiation

Read the following physiological effects observed in plants:
(i) Breaks seed and bud dormancy
(ii) Initiates germination in peanut seeds
(iii) Promotes sprouting of potato tubers
(iv) Promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants

Which of the following plant growth regulators is responsible for all the above effects?
questions.solution:
Ethylene is a gaseous plant growth regulator that performs all the listed functions.

While Gibberellic acid is generally associated with breaking dormancy and internode elongation, the specific examples of initiating germination in peanut seeds, sprouting of potato tubers, and rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants are characteristic physiological effects of Ethylene as per NCERT.

Auxins are primarily involved in apical dominance and root initiation, while Cytokinins promote cell division and delay leaf senescence.

Therefore, Ethylene is the correct answer.

Answer: Ethylene

Match List-I with List-II regarding the discovery of plant growth regulators.

(D) F. Skoog(IV) Rice seedlings

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The discovery of plant growth regulators involved several key scientists and plant materials:

Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed phototropism in the coleoptiles of canary grass.

F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

E. Kurosawa discovered gibberellins while studying the 'bakanae' disease in rice seedlings.

F. Skoog and his co-workers observed callus proliferation from the internodal segments of tobacco stems, leading to the discovery of cytokinins.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ethylene is a simple gaseous plant growth regulator with diverse physiological roles. Which of the following is NOT a physiological effect attributed to ethylene?
options: Promoting rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants
Promoting root growth and root hair formation
questions.solution:
Ethylene is a highly effective plant growth regulator that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes.

It breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, and causes sprouting of potato tubers.

It promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants, helping leaves or upper parts of the shoot to remain above water.

It also promotes root growth and root hair formation, thereby increasing the absorption surface of the plant.

However, overcoming apical dominance is a specific physiological effect of cytokinins, not ethylene. Therefore, the statement about overcoming apical dominance is the incorrect effect for ethylene.

Answer: Overcoming apical dominance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding a plant growth regulator that is widely used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns:

(A) It does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
(B) It promotes apical dominance.
(C) It promotes the abscission of young leaves and fruits.
(D) It induces parthenocarpy in tomatoes.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The plant growth regulator widely used to prepare weed-free lawns is auxin (specifically 2,4-D).

Statement (A) is correct. Auxins like 2,4-D selectively kill dicotyledonous weeds and do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.

Statement (B) is correct. In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance, which is mediated by auxins.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Auxins help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages (young leaves and fruits) but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

Statement (D) is correct. Auxins are known to induce parthenocarpy, for example, in tomatoes.

Therefore, three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.solution: Bacteria, fungi and lower plants survive in adverse conditions through formation of thick walled spores. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Plant growth as a whole is indefinite. 
Reason : Plants retain the capacity of continuous growth throughout their life.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Unlike animals, plants do not stop growing after reaching maturity. They continue to grow and bear new roots, leaves, branches, flowers, etc. While roots, stems and their branches have indefinite growth, other organs like leaves, flowers and fruits show limited or definite growth. They appear and fall off periodically and sometimes repeatedly. In lower plants, growth is diffused as every cell can divide and enlarge. Higher plants possess specific areas which take part in the formation of new cells. These areas are called meristems. Meristems are of three types- apical, intercalary and lateral. Cells of the meristematic region have the capacity to divide and self perpetuate. They produce cells which lose the capacity to divide and enter $G_0$ phase for undergoing differentiation to form particular tissues and organs. The meristem which is consumed in the formation of an organ is called determinate meristem. The meristem which continues its activity throughout life of the plant is called indeterminate meristem. It is the reason behind indefinite growth of plants.

Assertion : Vernalization is acceleration of subsquent flowering by low temperature treatment.
Reason : Site of vernalization is apical meristem.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Term vernalization was first given by T.D. Lysenko (1928). In colder countries, there are cereals of 2 physiological types, i.e., winter cereals and spring cereals. Winter cereals are sown in winter and flower in following summer whereas spring cereals are sown in spring and flower in summer. If winter cereal is sown in spring, it shows vegetative growth but does not flower unless it receives low temperature of winter. But winter cereal can be converted into spring cereal by providing artificial low temperature treatment, (i.e., springification.) Some plants requiring low temperature requirement (vernalization) for flowering are Secale cereale (European rye), Triticum vulgare, Brassica oleracea, Beta vulgaris, Apium and Lolium perenne, etc. Site of vernalization is apical meristem or all the meristematic cells. As a result of vernalization, a flowering hormone called "vernalin" is formed (reported by Melchers), but venalin has never been isolated. Once a plant is vernalized, it can be devernalized by exposing the plant to temperature of \(30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) or above. For establishing vernalization, plant should be kept at \(20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) for \(4-5\) days.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Avena curvature test is a bioassay for examining the activity of
questions.solution: Bioassay is a testing of biological activity like growth response of a substance by employing plant part. Avena curvature test is a bioassay for examining the activity of auxins. It is based upon experiments of Went. $10^{\circ}$ curvature is produced by auxin concentration of $150 \mu \mathrm{g} /$ lit at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $90 \%$ relative humidity. It can measure auxin upto 300 $\mu \mathrm{g}$ /itre. Auxin from shoot tip or any other plant organ is allowed to diffuse in a standard size agar block. 15 - $30 \mathrm{~mm}$ long oat coleoptile grown in dark is held vertically over water. $1 \mathrm{~mm}$ tip of coleoptile is removed without injuring the primary leaf. After 3 hours a second decapitation is carried out for $4 \mathrm{~mm}$ distance. Primary leaf is now pulled loose and agar block supported against it at the tip of decapitated coleoptile. After $90-110 \mathrm{~mm}$ the coleoptile is found to have bent. The curvature is measured.

questions.solution: Process of ageing is called senescence. Ageing, is cumulative changes in an organism, organ, tissue, or cell leading to a decrease in functional capacity. In humans, aging is associated with degenerative changes in the skin, bones, heart, blood vessels, lungs, nerves, and other organs and tissues. It is genetically controlled programme regulated by regulatory genes. This view is suggested by the great range of lifespans among different animal speciesfrom a few days in the fruit fly to more than 100 years in some tortoises. Scientists have recently learned how to double the lifespans of such laboratory organisms as roundworms and fruit flies through genetic manipulation, and mutant genes in mice have been observed to have a comparable effect in postponing ageing.

questions.solution: Flowering is a phytochrome regulated process. Phytotchrome is a blue protein pigment with a molecular mass of about $125 \mathrm{k} \mathrm{Da}$ (kilodaltons). As per 'Active $\mathrm{K}^{+}$transport mechanism' accumulation of $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions occurs in the guard cell during the day in response to light. It increases the turgidity of guard cells, consequently stomata open.
During night, ions move out of the guard cells into surrounding epidermal cells consequently guard cells become flaccid and stomata close.

questions.q: Apical dominance is caused by
questions.solution: In many plants, as the apical bud grows, the growth of lower axillary buds is suppressed. Removal of apical bud results in the growth of lower buds. The auxin (IAA) of the terminal bud inhibits the growth of lateral buds. This phenomenon is known as apical dominance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following plant is LDP ?
questions.solution: Long Day Plants (LDP) require a photoperiod of more than a critical length, which may vary from 4 to 18 hours. The best flowering of long day plants usually occurs in continuous light. For flowering they require either no dark period or a very short dark period. Example of long day plants are wheat, maize, oats, spinach etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a day neutral plant?
questions.solution: Day neutral plants do not need a specific photoperiod to produce flowers. They are also called intermediates or photoneutrals. Their photoperiod varies from a few hours to 24 hours of uninterrupted light e.g. tomato, cucumber, sunflower, Helianthus annuus, maize and cotton etc.
